attempted_claim: For the binary segmented single-deletion channel with segment length 32 and blocklength N=1024, every block-by-block decodable code with block error probability at most 1e-3 has information rate at most 0.78 bits per channel use, where the 0.78 ceiling decomposes into a memoryless information-spectrum outage term plus an explicit per-segment marker-uncertainty penalty that vanishes when boundaries are revealed; the upper bound R*(1024,1e-3)<=0.78 is the TARGET.
claim_type: finite-blocklength information-spectrum converse with marker overhead
decisive_failure: No full converse was proved: the marker tax was certified only for a fixed single-bit-marker construction rather than all block-by-block resync strategies, the log2(33) packing overhead used is a zero-error figure whose finite-error correction is unquantified, and the information-spectrum outage term was only heuristically estimated near 0.89 via Monte Carlo, so the 0.78 ceiling remains undecided and the partial certificate is preserved for future work.
